reasons: Reproduced: variant compiles; trigger NumberUtilsTest::testToByteString fails with 'toByte(String) 2 failed'; the full suite has exactly that one failure; all five ownership tests pass. (a) Only the gold's own code breaks its contract: toSignedInt is documented to parse the range 'as a decimal number' and to reject values above limit, yet it adds Character.digit's -1 for a non-digit as if it were a digit ("abc" -> -111, "1a" -> 9, "12a" -> 119, all confirmed by probe); facade, hop 1 and hop 4 are wrong on "abc" only by inheritance, hops 2 and 3 do exactly what their javadoc says. (b) Each hop's javadoc matches its code; hop 2 documents precisely the sign and empty/sign-alone rules it implements (the Integer.parseInt split), hop 3 documents the sign-dependent magnitude, hop 4 is a delegating copy of the gold's contract. (c) No competing repair: the gold fix restores Byte.parseByte behaviour on all 24 probe inputs; hop-1 Byte.parseByte is a bypass (hops 2-5 dead); hop-2 and hop-4 isNumeric pre-filters pass everything and are behaviourally complete but re-implement the gold's per-character decision ahead of it and leave the gold's documented contract violated (toSignedInt("abc",...) = -111), so they are bypasses; hop-2 first-character, hop-3 sign-check and hop-3 clamp edits pass the suite but are test-fitted and contradict the toShort/toInt/isDigits convention. (d) Names are neutral, no fault vocabulary; the lie describes a different accumulation order and names neither the fault, the omitted digit check nor a hop. (e) Gold is five calls below toByte(String,byte); hops are in five distinct existing classes (DateUtils, SystemUtils, ToStringStyle, StringUtils, ArrayUtils); facade is guard + one delegating call; one added procedural sentence the facade does not perform; gold javadoc silent on non-digit rejection; existing trigger, empty test.patch, sole new failure; one-line omission. (f) Convention pinned outside the gold by NumberUtils.toShort/toInt (JDK parsers, default for 'abc' and '1234.5'), NumberUtils.isDigits (rejects '1ab', 'abc') and passing tests testToShortString, testToShortStringI, testToIntString, testIsDigits, testToByteStringI ('12.3' -> default).
notes: Bypasses recorded: (1) hop 1 'return Byte.parseByte(str);'; (2) hop 2 'if (start == str.length() || !StringUtils.isNumeric(str.substring(start))) {'; (3) hop 4 isNumeric pre-check before the delegating return. The pre-filters (2) and (3) are the closest to competing repairs: they are one-line, pass the full suite and match Byte.parseByte on every probed input (including Unicode digits and sign combinations). They are classed as bypasses because they duplicate the gold's per-character accept/reject decision and leave ArrayUtils.toSignedInt, a public method documented to parse a decimal number, returning -111 for "abc". The BUILD_BRIEF asks for a fault 'no caller can pre-filter or recover'; recovery is impossible here ("1a" -> 9 is indistinguishable from "9"), but a whole-input pre-check by a caller is possible; reviewers may want to keep that in mind. Hop 2 is the most plausible alternative owner (it is the syntax-check layer), but its javadoc limits its rule to sign and emptiness and the gold is where Character.digit's -1 is consumed unchecked. Cosmetic: the lie line is appended after '@since 2.5' without a leading '*', so in rendered javadoc it attaches to the @since tag; it does not name the fault or the gold. Harness note: copying a compiled tree and editing within a second leaves stale classes under ant's 1 s timestamp granularity; all alternative runs were redone after deleting target/.
